claim.citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Cambridge University Press, Ch. XVII 'On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms', pp. 757-759, Figs. 388-393
claim.text_as_registered: The pelves of Archaeopteryx and Apatornis (after Heilmann) and intermediate configurations can be found by interpolation between coordinate-transformed forms - i.e. interpolated grids generate biologically real intermediate forms.
claim.text_as_printed: In Fig. 390 the outlines of these two co-ordinate systems are superposed upon one another, and those of three intermediate and equidistant co-ordinate systems are interpolated between them. From each of these latter systems, so determined by direct interpolation, a complete co-ordinate diagram is drawn, and the corresponding outline of a pelvis is found from each of these systems of co-ordinates, as in Figs. 391, 392. Finally, in Fig. 393 the complete series is represented, beginning with the known pelvis of Archaeopteryx, and leading up by our three intermediate hypothetical types to the known pelvis of Apatornis. (p. 759)

decomposition.A_methodological: Three equidistant interpolations of the Archaeopteryx->Apatornis coordinate transformation yield well-defined intermediate pelvis outlines (Heilmann's Figs. 391-393). Testable from Thompson's own figures.
decomposition.B_biological_reality: Those interpolated intermediates are 'biologically real' (match actual phylogenetically intermediate Mesozoic bird pelves). Thompson himself only calls them 'hypothetical types' and 'transitional stages'. Requires landmark data of real intermediate taxa, which the pinned data do not supply.

openalex.finding: No open 2-D landmark dataset of Mesozoic bird pelves spanning Archaeopteryx -> Apatornis was found; the biological-reality half of the claim therefore remains untestable in this loop.

collision_check.result: no collision; all files created by this loop are new and uniquely named

method_summary: Segment the five silhouettes of Fig. 393 (Otsu threshold, morphological opening, connected components); extract boundaries; detect the acetabulum and four process tips as landmarks; place arc-length semilandmarks; fit the Archaeopteryx->Apatornis coordinate transformation (thin-plate spline, with affine-only control) and generate the three equidistant interpolated forms x_t = (1-t) x + t phi(x), t = 1/4, 1/2, 3/4; compare against Heilmann's drawn intermediates by Procrustes distance, IoU and best-fit t*, with endpoint-copy and shuffled-t null controls.
